requirement:
HC represents a FIXME acknowledgment as a graph node and exposes its tracking
issue relationships as labeled edges to GitHub issue nodes. A named FIXME also
connects the acknowledgment to the requirement whose gap it acknowledges;
an unnamed FIXME connects directly to its tracking issues.
Each issue named by the acknowledgment is available through its tracking edges.
rationale:
`requirements.sdk.habeas.fixme_graph` requires four things. A FIXME acknowledgment is a graph node. Its tracking-issue relationships are labeled edges to GitHub issue nodes. A named FIXME also connects to the requirement it acknowledges, while an unnamed FIXME connects directly to its issues. Every issue the acknowledgment names is reachable through those edges.

`references` returns no {test} or {impl} sites for the requirement, so no reviewed test covers any of these obligations. The named and unnamed cases, source ownership, and multiple issue targets are all untested.

The one nearby test I found is `src/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[domain_storage_round_trips_each_review_kind_and_preserves_records_on_errors]`. It only stores a review record whose `fixmes` list is empty. It does not check graph nodes or edges.

The gap is acknowledged. `src/sdk.rs#enum[HabeasNode]` carries a {fixme} reference to `requirements.sdk.habeas.fixme_graph` that names nikomatsakis/habeas-codicem#26, which is open. Its body says the graph nodes and tracking edges are deferred and that the named, unnamed, source-ownership and multiple-issue cases have no tests. That matches the missing tests. The gap still exists, so the acknowledgment is not stale.
